basis.text: The licence looked up is ABC Type 47 (on-sale general, eating place), as stated in the description.
The licence is to be obtained by transfer from other premises (a premises-to-premises transfer), as the applicant states.

A Type 47 licence is an on-sale general licence. State law limits these to one for each 2,000 inhabitants of the county; in a county over that number ABC issues no additional one, so the licence comes by transfer of an existing licence unless state law allows otherwise.

North Beach Special Use District (repealed 2025-12-15): A Restaurant may sell beer, wine or liquor for drinking on the premises (ABC licence Types 02, 23, 41, 47, 49, 59 or 75) only by Conditional Use on the First Story, with a Planning Commission finding that it is and will remain a Bona Fide Eating Place. Here: a conditional use (Planning Code § 780.3(c)(2)(A), in force since before 2022-01-01 until 2025-12-14).

North Beach Special Use District (repealed 2025-12-15): To show it is still a Bona Fide Eating Place, the Restaurant had to give the Department, on request, records showing that at least 51% of its gross receipts in the preceding year came from food prepared and sold to guests on the premises. This is a requirement, not a control (Planning Code § 780.3(c)(2)(A), in force since before 2022-01-01 until 2024-01-13).
Census tract 106.00: 52 active on-sale retail licences in ABC's licences as they stood on 9 March 2022, against 12 authorised in ABC's census tract authorisations of September 2026.

The tract is over its authorised number, and state law tests a transfer from other premises for undue concentration. The licence may still issue if public convenience or necessity would be served: public convenience or necessity finding likely required.

The liquor licence rule of the restricted district makes this licence a conditional use here, so it can be used only with a Conditional Use Authorization. ABC also investigates the application, and the applicant must post public notice: further review.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC agency referral approved September 2017 at 431 Columbus Avenue (53 m away, same block) for continuation of an existing Type 47 license. This is an agency referral (not a CUA), but it cites prior CPC Motion No. 16916, confirming that Type 47 is permitted for bona fide eating places in the North Beach NCD and SUD under Sections 722 and 780.3.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning's approval letter confirms that a Type 47 license 'is permitted in conjunction with a Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place' in North Beach, and that continuation of an existing Type 47 is routine. This signals that once a Type 47 is approved via CUA, transfers and renewals are handled administratively as agency referrals, not new CUAs.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC agency referral approved October 2019 at 1512 Stockton Street (105 m away, North Beach NCD) for an existing established restaurant with an existing Type 47 license (#343850). Another agency referral showing routine approval of Type 47 continuation.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline of 120 to 300 days and cost of $3,100 to $465,000 are for approvals granted: the Conditional Use Authorization (120 to 300 days from filing to approval, $3,100 to $15,000 depending on construction cost, per the catalog and comparable CUA filings in North Beach), the ABC Type 47 premises-to-premises transfer (90 to 240 days including escrow, posting, ABC investigation, and city referrals; $17,000 to $450,000 for the license purchase on the open market plus $1,000 to $1,600 in ABC fees), and the health permit to operate (14 to 45 days, $470 to $1,000). The CUA is the critical path: comparable CUA filings at 1318 Grant (2015-000635CUA) took 159 days from filing to approval. ABC transfer timelines depend on undue-concentration review; if ABC requires a public convenience or necessity finding from the Board of Supervisors, add 60 to 120 days to the ABC timeline. The cost range reflects the Type 47 license purchase price, which dominates the total; the applicant should confirm current market prices through an ABC broker before committing to the lease. These figures do not include denial or withdrawal; the nine comparable approvals in the precedent set took 9 to 159 days, all approved. Business registration, entity formation, seller's permit, RBS training, food handler cards, food safety manager certification, and music licenses add 1 to 35 days and $635 to $3,385 in fees, but those are not entitlement approvals and are handled in parallel.

records_summary: 414 Columbus Ave is in the North Beach NCD where restaurants are conditional uses on the first story and may only be approved in spaces last legally occupied by a restaurant or bar. The records show this address has operated as "Original U.S. Restaurant" continuously since at least 1986, with an active Type 41 license since 2016 and three prior CUAs (1986, 1998, 2010) that added entertainment and upgraded the license from Type 41 to Type 47. The 1987 CUA (Case No. 1986.553C) specifically approved replacing the beer & wine license with a full liquor license "with no change in operation, furniture fixtures, or building." Within 500 feet there are 60 registered food and drink businesses including 12 bars, 40 active on-sale ABC licenses, and 97 total on-sale licenses within 1,000 feet—flagging possible undue concentration. The block has approved numerous restaurant continuations and license upgrades; five dated use decisions in the last five years were all approved, though the sample is too small for a rate.
